That work fixed pages that double-wrapped a component's own sizing, but left several pages alone as "legitimate page-authored content". A full repo grep (`grep -rl "from '@mantine'" src/app --include="page.tsx"`) shows the real scope is much larger: **23 page.tsx files** import directly from Mantine, not 5.

**Goal:** generalise the rule fully — a `page.tsx` should only fetch data, wire up server actions, and compose components; it should never itself import from `@mantine/core` or any other Mantine package.

**Scope, grouped by pattern:**

1. **Static page-authored content → own component.** No reusable data component to fold sizing into; the page IS the content. Extract each into a dedicated component: `rules`, `familytree` (Flex/Title/Text wrapper around the existing `FamilyTree` component), `tables`, `countrymap`, `info`, `footy/page.tsx` (home page hero), `docs/admin`, `docs/migration` (small shared wrapper for the two MDX pages).
2. **Single-component wrap with no sizing of its own** — same gap as `NewGameForm` had before this audit. `turnout/page.tsx` wraps `Turnout` in `Stack w="100%" p="xl" align="center"`; fold that into `Turnout` itself, page becomes a Fragment.
3. **Repeated "year page shell" pattern** — `winners`, `books`, `curse`, `games`, and `table/[table]` all duplicate the same `Group justify="center"><TitleWithYearDropdown .../></Group>` (plus an outer `Stack`/`Flex`) around one data component. This is a strong candidate for a single shared component (e.g. a `YearPageHeading` or similar) rather than five near-identical copies of the same Mantine layout.
4. **Repeated error/status notification pattern** — `auth/accountdeleted`, `auth/reset-password` (missing-token branch), `auth/claim/[token]` (invalid-invitation branch), `downloadmydata` (two branches), `profile` (two branches), and `admin/users` (fetch-error branch) all render a `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red"/"blue">{message}</Notification>` (or, for `response/page.tsx`, a `Box`+`Text`+`Anchor` variant) directly in the page. Extract a single shared component (e.g. `StatusNotification`) covering both shapes rather than duplicating the pattern seven times.
5. **Genuine multi-component composition needing its own wrapper** — `admin/page.tsx` (dashboard: two independent admin widgets in a `Flex`) and `game/[id]/page.tsx` (`GameDaySummary` + conditional `GameResultForm` in a `Flex`) each arrange more than one component together. This is legitimate page-level composition (per the SYS-586 council verdict), but it still means the page imports Mantine directly — give each its own dedicated wrapper component so the page itself stays Mantine-free.

**Also still in scope from the original ticket:**

* Extend the existing ESLint override at `eslint.config.mjs` (`files: ["src/app/**/page.{ts,tsx}"]`, which already bans the `'use client'` directive in pages via `no-restricted-syntax`) with a `no-restricted-imports` rule banning `@mantine/*` imports in page files, so the rule is enforced mechanically rather than by convention/review.

**Acceptance criteria:**

* No `page.tsx` in `src/app/**` imports from any `@mantine/*` package; enforced by an ESLint rule, not just documented.
* Every page above renders via a dedicated component (new or extended), each with its own test coverage matching the codebase's component-test conventions: accessible selectors, real Mantine rendering, no reliance on Mantine internals.
* `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npx knip` all clean.

content.text:
Looked at SYS-600 and the current ESLint config — worth noting the ban isn't live yet (only the `'use client'` restriction is enforced today in the pages override); the `no-restricted-imports` rule for `@mantine/*` in pages is what this ticket proposes adding.

My take: keep the blanket ban. The RSC dot-notation bug itself doesn't require it (that only bites property access on a `'use client'` export, so a page importing `Flex` directly and composing two components inside it wouldn't trigger it) — but the real value is that "pages only fetch, wire actions, and compose" becomes mechanically enforceable rather than a per-PR judgment call, which matches how this codebase already handles the client/server split (categorical rule over case-by-case exception, per the `require-use-client` rationale in CLAUDE.md). The cost is genuinely minor boilerplate for case 5 in the ticket (`admin/page.tsx`, `game/[id]/page.tsx`) — a one-line `Flex` wrapping two components now needs its own wrapper file and test, even though nothing there is reusable or complex enough to *need* isolation on its own merits.

Want me to start on the extraction work, or do you want to revisit the ticket's scope first?
How many pages would need to change? How many new components needed?

Verified against the current tree (not just the ticket text, which is 2 weeks old): **23 `page.tsx` files** still import from `@mantine/*` and would need to change — same number the ticket cites, confirmed by `grep -rl "from '@mantine" src/app --include="page.tsx"`.

Two things the ticket mentions have already been resolved on `main`:
- `game/[id]/page.tsx` — already a pure Fragment (`AutoRefresh` + `GameDaySummary`), the exact pattern group 5 asks for.
- `docs/admin` / `docs/migration` — already import only their `.mdx` content, no Mantine import in the page itself, so no wrapper needed there.

For the 23 remaining, grouped by the ticket's own categories and re-verified by grep:

| Group | Pages | New components |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Own dedicated component (static content) | `rules`, `familytree`, `tables`, `countrymap`, `info`, `footy/page.tsx` (home) — 6 | 6 (one each) |
| 2. Fold into existing component | `turnout` — 1 | 0 (edit `Turnout` itself) |
| 3. Shared "year page shell" | `winners`, `books`, `curse`, `games`, `table/[table]` — 5 | 1 (`YearPageHeading` or similar) |
| 4. Shared status-notification | `auth/accountdeleted`, `auth/reset-password`, `auth/claim/[token]`, `auth/claim/[token]/finish`, `auth/verify/enquiry/[token]`, `auth/verify/extra-email/[token]`, `downloadmydata`, `profile`, `admin/users`, `response/[token]` — 10 | 1 (`StatusNotification`, covering both the `Notification` and `Box+Text+Anchor` shapes) |
| 5. Dedicated wrapper, genuine composition | `admin` (dashboard) — 1 | 1 |

**Totals: 23 pages changed, 9 new components** (plus the ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule extension itself).

Note groups 1–2 & 4's real per-page count came out slightly different from the ticket's prose (which undercounted the notification group — it's 10, not 7, once `claim/[token]/finish`, `verify/enquiry`, and `verify/extra-email` are included) but the total of 23 pages still matches.

- `<Notification icon={<IconX .../>} color="blue">` (note: blue, not red — this is an informational, not error, notification, despite using `IconX`) wrapping `<Text>Your account has been successfully deleted.</Text>`.
- No `withCloseButton` prop set (defaults true). No anchor. Notification is the ONLY content on the page.

**2. `src/app/footy/auth/reset-password/page.tsx`**
- Conditional on `token` presence (from `searchParams`).
- Failure branch: `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red">` + `<Text>Password reset link is missing or invalid.</Text>`. No `withCloseButton` prop. No anchor. Sole content.
- Success branch: renders `<PasswordResetForm token={token} />` (no Mantine, not a notification at all).

**3. `src/app/footy/auth/claim/[token]/page.tsx`**
- Calls `claimPlayerInvitation(token)` in try/catch; captures error via `captureUnexpectedError`; `errorMessage = toPublicMessage(error, 'This invitation link is invalid.')`.
- Failure branch (`!invitation`): `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red" withCloseButton={false}>{errorMessage}</Notification>` — message is a **variable** (dynamic string), not literal JSX/Text wrapper (children passed directly, no `<Text>`). Sole content, no anchor.
- Success branch: renders `<ClaimSignup name={...} email={...} token={...} />` — not a notification.

**4. `src/app/footy/auth/claim/[token]/finish/page.tsx`**
- Calls `finalizePlayerInvitationClaim(token)`; catches, sets `errorMessage` via `toPublicMessage(error, 'Unable to finalize invitation.')`.
- Failure branch: `<Stack>` wrapping `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red" withCloseButton={false}>{errorMessage}</Notification>` **plus** `<Anchor href="/footy">Return to the home page</Anchor>` as a sibling.
- Success branch: `redirect('/footy/profile')` (no JSX rendered at all on success).
- Notification is NOT the only content here — always paired with an `Anchor` inside a `Stack`.

**5. `src/app/footy/auth/verify/enquiry/[token]/page.tsx`**
- Calls `deliverContactEnquiry(token)`; catches, `errorMessage = toPublicMessage(error, 'Unable to deliver your message.')`.
- Failure branch: `<Stack>` + `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red" withCloseButton={false}>{errorMessage}</Notification>` + `<Anchor href="/footy">Return to the home page</Anchor>`.
- Success branch (no errorMessage): `<Stack>` + `<Notification icon={<IconCheck/>} color="teal" withCloseButton={false}>Thanks for your message. We will get back to you soon.</Notification>` + `<Anchor href="/footy">Return to the home page</Anchor>`.
- This is the only file with BOTH a success notification (green/teal + check icon) and a failure notification, each paired with the same anchor. Confirms the pattern needs a `color`/`icon` that varies for success vs failure, plus a literal message string for success and dynamic string for failure.

**6. `src/app/footy/auth/verify/extra-email/[token]/page.tsx`**
- Calls `verifyEmail(token)`; catches, `errorMessage = toPublicMessage(error, 'Unable to verify email.')`.
- Failure branch: `<Stack>` + `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red" withCloseButton={false}>{errorMessage}</Notification>` + `<Anchor href="/footy/profile">Return to your profile</Anchor>` (different href/label than #4/#5 — "Return to your profile").
- Success branch: `redirect('/footy/profile')`, no JSX.

**7. `src/app/footy/(authenticated)/downloadmydata/page.tsx`**
- Two independent failure branches, both plain `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red">` (no `withCloseButton` prop set — defaults true, unlike files 3/4/5/6 which explicitly set `false`):
  - No `playerId` (from `getCurrentUser()`): children = literal JSX text `This account is not linked to a player profile yet.` (no `<Text>` wrapper, no variable).
  - `!player` after fetching: children = literal `Failed to load player data.`
- No anchor in either branch; each Notification is the sole content.
- Success branch: builds a `payload` object and renders `<DownloadMyData data={serialisedPayload} />` — not a notification, substantial data-fetch/transform logic (5 parallel service calls + totals computation).

**8. `src/app/footy/(authenticated)/profile/page.tsx`**
- Structurally identical pattern to #7: two failure branches with plain `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red">` (no `withCloseButton`), literal text children (`This account is not linked to a player profile yet.` and `Failed to load player profile.`), no anchor, sole content each.
- Success branch: renders `<><AutoRefresh channels={FootyChannel.Players} /><PlayerProfileForm .../></>` — not a notification.

**9. `src/app/footy/admin/users/page.tsx`**
- Different variant: uses `<Text c="red">{toPublicMessage(error, 'Failed to fetch users.')}</Text>` directly — NOT a `Notification` component at all, no icon, no color prop on a Notification (just Mantine `Text` color prop). This is the "Box+Text" style variant referenced in the prompt (though it's bare `Text`, no `Box`/`Anchor`).
- Triggered inside a try/catch around `listUsersAction()`.
- Success branch: `<><AutoRefresh channels={FootyChannel.Users} /><AdminUserList users={users} setAdminRole={setAdminRoleAction} /></>`.
- Structural outlier: no icon, no `Notification` wrapper — just colored text.

**10. `src/app/footy/response/[token]/page.tsx`**
- Another outlier: no `Notification` at all. Uses `<Text>Invitation details are missing.</Text>` + `<Anchor href="/footy/game">Go to the game page</Anchor>` inside a fragment `<>...</>` when `getGameInvitationResponseDetails(token)` returns falsy. No icon, no color prop anywhere.
- Success branch: renders `<GameInvitationResponseForm details={details} onSubmitGameInvitationResponse={submitGameInvitationResponse} />`.

### Assessment: can one `StatusNotification` component cover all 10?

Not cleanly with a single trivial `{message, color, icon, variant, anchor}` API — there are real structural differences to account for:

- **Two distinct rendering families**: `Notification`-based (files 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 — 8 of 10) vs plain `Text`(+`Anchor`)-based with no icon/notification chrome at all (files 9 and 10). A shared component would need a `variant: 'notification' | 'text'` prop (matching the "Box+Text+Anchor variant" the prompt anticipated) to cover 9 and 10, or those two could reasonably be left out of the shared component (they're not really the same visual pattern — no icon, no colored notification box).
- **`withCloseButton`**: explicitly `false` in files 3,4,5,6; left at default (`true`) in files 1,2,7,8. Needs to be a prop (default true, override false) — not a hardcoded constant.
- **Anchor is optional and varies**: absent in 1,2,3,7,8,9(has one)/10(has one); present in 4,5,6 (all `red`/error) each with different `href`/label (`/footy` "Return to the home page" ×2, `/footy/profile` "Return to your profile"); present in 9/10 style too. So `anchor?: { href: string; label: string }` fits well for the `Notification`-family files that have one (4, 5, 6) plus the two `Text` outliers (9 doesn't have an anchor, 10 does).
- **Message content type varies**: literal hardcoded JSX text (1, 7, 8) vs dynamic string variables from `toPublicMessage()` (3, 4, 5 error branch, 6, 9). A `message: React.ReactNode` prop handles both.
- **Color/icon pairing varies**: `red`+`IconX` (2,3,4,5 err,6,7,8), `blue`+`IconX` (1 — non-error info), `teal`+`IconCheck` (5 success). So `color` and `icon` must be independent props, not derived from a single `severity` enum, unless you add a `'blue'` info variant.
- **Wrapping context differs**: standalone (1,2,3,7,8) vs wrapped in `<Stack>` with a sibling `<Anchor>` (4,5,6) — but this is just consumption-side layout, easily handled by having the shared component itself optionally render the anchor internally (via the `anchor` prop) rather than requiring callers to wrap in `Stack`.
- **File 5 is the only site needing two calls of the component** (error state and success state) in the same page — not a structural blocker, just confirms the component must support both colors/icons via props rather than being error-only.
- **Files 9 and 10 have no icon/Notification chrome at all** — forcing them into a `Notification`-styled shared component would change their visual appearance unless the component supports a `variant='plain'` (bare colored `Text` + optional `Anchor`, no `Notification` box) as literally the "Box+Text+Anchor" variant mentioned in your prompt.

**Conclusion**: A `StatusNotification` component with props like `{ variant: 'notification' | 'plain', message: ReactNode, color: MantineColor, icon?: ReactNode, withCloseButton?: boolean, anchor?: { href: string; label: string } }` would cover all 10 call sites structurally, but note it's genuinely two different visual variants (8 Notification-box sites + 2 plain-Text sites), and files 7/8 have identical dual-branch logic that could even share a slightly higher-level "PlayerNotLinked" pattern on top of the base component. No site has additional non-trivial JSX inside the notification itself beyond text/variable content, so the "message" prop as `ReactNode` is sufficient everywhere.</result>

'use client';

import { Anchor, Container, Flex, Text, Title } from '@mantine/core';

import { EnquiryForm } from '@/components/EnquiryForm/EnquiryForm';
import { SendEnquiryProxy } from '@/types/actions/SendEnquiry';

export interface Props {
    onSendEnquiry: SendEnquiryProxy;
}

export const InfoContent = ({ onSendEnquiry }: Props) => {
    return (
        <Flex
            gap="md"
            align="flex-start"
            direction="column"
            p="xl"
        >
            <Title order={1}>Toastboy FC: Tuesday Night Football</Title>
            <Text>
                We play a friendly five-a-side footy game amongst ourselves
                every Tuesday night between 6 and 7pm at the{' '}
                <Anchor href="http://www.kelseykerridge.co.uk/">
                    Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre
                </Anchor>{' '}
                in Cambridge (for our international visitors, that's
                "soccer", "center" and "Cambridge, England").
            </Text>
            <Container fluid>
                <iframe
                    src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d2445.3263160975907!2d0.1279577126825085!3d52.20111725967227!2m3!1f0!2f0!3f0!3m2!1i1024!2i768!4f13.1!3m3!1m2!1s0x47d8709a9a53b7ff%3A0x34e196dca006ac25!2sKelsey%20Kerridge%20Sports%20Centre!5e0!3m2!1sen!2suk!4v1716736866954!5m2!1sen!2suk"
                    width="100%"
                    height="450"
                    allowFullScreen={true}
                    title="Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre"
                    referrerPolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"
                />
            </Container>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/rules">
                    Here's an outline of the rules of our games.
                </Anchor>{' '}
                The standard of play's not too high, although we're not
                complete duffers - but we do play to win. After all, there's
                the glory of the trophies which are presented at the
                sumptuous end-of-year awards ceremonies at stake. Here's how
                it works. Every player who's on the winning team each week
                gets 3 points, or 1 for a draw. There are 3 trophies up for
                grabs:
            </Text>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/points">Points</Anchor>. Simple -
                whoever has the biggest points total at the end of the year
                wins the Pewterware.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/averages">Averages</Anchor>. Just the
                points total divided by the number of games played, but note
                you have to have played a minimum of 5 games in a year to
                qualify.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/stalwart">Stalwart</Anchor>. To
                encourage people to play regularly. The winner is the one
                who's played the most games in a year.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                Each week an automated email goes out, inviting players to
                log in to the site and say whether or not they can play. Once
                we have enough players, we run the picker script which picks
                the fairest possible teams based on the age and number of
                wins in the last 10 games played of each player. I ask for
                four pounds fifty from each player to cover the cost of the
                hall booking and things like footballs and bibs. We nearly
                always go for a pint after the game: everyone is welcome. We
                usually go to the Grain and Hop Store and then often for a
                bite to eat.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                There's an extra little bonus something at the award ceremony
                for the person who has the best average response time
                throughout the year: keep track of where you stand in the{' '}
                <Anchor href="/footy/speedy">Captain Speedy</Anchor> table.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                We're always looking for players, so if you want to join the
                list, fill in the form below!
            </Text>
            <EnquiryForm onSendEnquiry={onSendEnquiry} />
        </Flex>
    );
};

All 23 pages, the ESLint rule, and 10 new components (including `WinnersGrid`, a small addition beyond the original plan to extract winners' per-table grid layout) are in place, with full test coverage. Final verification summary:

- **`npm run typecheck`** — clean

- **`npm run format:check`** — clean
- **`npx knip`** — clean, no unused files/exports
- **`npm run test`** (full suite: actions, api, components, pages, services, lib) — 238 files, 1978 tests passed (1 pre-existing skip, 4 pre-existing todos)
- **Components layer coverage** — 100% statements/branches/functions/lines
- **Pages layer coverage** — 97.3% statements (uncovered lines are pre-existing, in files I didn't touch)

One deviation from the plan worth flagging: `winners/page.tsx` needed an extra `WinnersGrid` component (not in the original 9) to absorb the `Flex`-wrapped map over multiple `WinnersTable` instances — that JSX couldn't fold into `YearPageShell` (it's winners-specific) or `WinnersTable` (which renders one table, not a grid) cleanly, so it got its own small wrapper. That brings the total to **10 new components** instead of 9.

I didn't run `npm run build` (it requires `op run --env-file ./.env --` for secrets you'd need to authorize) — the finalisation checklist's required steps (typecheck/lint/format/knip) plus the full test suite all pass, so I'd suggest running the build yourself when convenient to get the last word before deploying.

input.summary: Silence Vite "configLoader: native" ESM-in-CommonJS warning on vitest config files
input.description:
Every `npm run test*` invocation prints one warning per vitest config file loaded, e.g.:

```
(!) Your Vite config uses features that are unsupported by `configLoader: 'native'`, which is planned to become the default in a future major version of Vite:
  - ESM syntax in a file loaded as CommonJS (vitest.unit.config.ts:1:1). Use a `.mjs` extension or set `"type": "module"` in the closest package.json
Set `VITE_CONFIG_NATIVE_IGNORE_WARNING=true` to suppress this warning.
```

**Cause:** `package.json` has no `"type": "module"` field, so it defaults to CommonJS. All of the repo's `vitest.*.config.ts` files use ESM `import` syntax (e.g. `import path from 'node:path';`), which Vite's upcoming default `configLoader: 'native'` doesn't support for CJS-mode `.ts` files.

**Affected files** (all currently loaded by at least one `npm run test*` script):
- `vitest.config.ts`
- `vitest.unit.config.ts`
- `vitest.actions.config.ts`
- `vitest.api.config.ts`
- `vitest.components.config.ts`
- `vitest.pages.config.ts`
- `vitest.lib.config.ts`
- `vitest.services.config.ts`
- `vitest.picker.integration.config.ts`

**Suggested fix:** rename each `vitest.*.config.ts` to `vitest.*.config.mts` (the narrower fix Vite itself suggests) rather than adding `"type": "module"` to `package.json`, since the latter is repo-wide and could affect unrelated CommonJS-assuming tooling. This requires updating:
1. The `--config vitest.*.config.ts` flag in every matching script in `package.json` (`test`, `test:watch`, `test:coverage`, `test:actions[:coverage]`, `test:api[:coverage]`, `test:components[:coverage]`, `test:pages[:coverage]`, `test:lib[:coverage]`, `test:services[:coverage]`, `test:picker:integration`).
2. The `projects: [...]` array of sibling config filenames inside `vitest.unit.config.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Running any `npm run test*` script produces no `configLoader: 'native'` / ESM-in-CommonJS warning.
- All test suites still pass with the renamed config files (`npm run test`, `npm run test:pages`, `npm run test:components`, etc.).
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, and `npx knip` remain clean.

- `vitest.config.ts`
- `vitest.unit.config.ts`
- `vitest.actions.config.ts`
- `vitest.api.config.ts`
- `vitest.components.config.ts`
- `vitest.pages.config.ts`
- `vitest.lib.config.ts`
- `vitest.services.config.ts`
- `vitest.picker.integration.config.ts`

**Suggested fix:** rename each `vitest.*.config.ts` to `vitest.*.config.mts` (the narrower fix Vite itself suggests) rather than adding `"type": "module"` to `package.json`, since the latter is repo-wide and could affect unrelated CommonJS-assuming tooling. This requires updating:
1. The `--config vitest.*.config.ts` flag in every matching script in `package.json` (`test`, `test:watch`, `test:coverage`, `test:actions[:coverage]`, `test:api[:coverage]`, `test:components[:coverage]`, `test:pages[:coverage]`, `test:lib[:coverage]`, `test:services[:coverage]`, `test:picker:integration`).
2. The `projects: [...]` array of sibling config filenames inside `vitest.unit.config.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Running any `npm run test*` script produces no `configLoader: 'native'` / ESM-in-CommonJS warning.
- All test suites still pass with the renamed config files (`npm run test`, `npm run test:pages`, `npm run test:components`, etc.).
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, and `npx knip` remain clean.

The ticket recommends renaming them to `.mts` (Vite's own suggested narrow fix) rather than flipping `package.json` to `"type": "module"` repo-wide, and lists the `package.json` scripts and the `projects` array in `vitest.unit.config.ts` that need their filenames updated to match.

Storybook's vitest addon resets `fn()` mocks between story runs, so a `.mockResolvedValue` set only at module scope gets wiped before the story actually renders. `AdminUpdatePlayerRecords.stories.tsx` handles this with a per-story `beforeEach` — matching that.

Two full-suite runs showed intermittent `Test timed out in 15000ms` failures on `WinnersTable` and `YearTable` (and transiently a wider set of unrelated stories on a contended run) — none of these are components I touched or introduced; it's headless-Chromium resource contention in this sandbox, not a regression from this work.

input.summary: Fix duplicate React keys from defaultPlayerRecordDataList mock fixture
input.description:
Any Storybook story or test that renders multiple rows from `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` (`src/tests/mocks/data/playerRecordData.ts`) triggers a React console error:

```
Encountered two children with the same key, `1`. Keys should be unique so that components maintain their identity across updates. Non-unique keys may cause children to be duplicated and/or omitted — the behavior is unsupported and could change in a future version.
```

**Root cause:** `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` is generated as:

```ts
export const defaultPlayerRecordDataList: PlayerRecordDataType[] = Array.from(
    { length: 20 },
    (_, index) =>
        createMockPlayerRecordData({
            points: 100 - 3 * index,
        }),
);
```

`createMockPlayerRecordData` only overrides `points`; every other field — including `id: 1` and `player: defaultPlayer` — comes from `defaultPlayerRecordData`/`defaultPlayerRecord` (`src/tests/mocks/data/playerRecord.ts`) unchanged. So all 20 generated records share the same `id` and the same `player`. Components that key rows by `record.id` (`WinnersTable`, and by extension anything reusing this fixture, e.g. `RecordsTable`, `YearTable`, and the new `HomeContent`/`WinnersGrid` from SYS-600) collide on that key.

Note `playerRecord.ts` already has a properly-varied 100-record fixture, `defaultPlayerRecordList` (unique `id`, varied `playerId`/`year`/stats per entry) — `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` just doesn't follow the same pattern when it wraps those records with `player` data for `PlayerRecordDataType` consumers.

**Suggested fix:** vary `id` (and ideally `playerId`/`player`) per generated entry in `defaultPlayerRecordDataList`, matching the existing pattern in `defaultPlayerRecordList`, so each of the 20 records is genuinely distinct rather than differing only in `points`.

**Affected consumers (currently emit the warning today):**
- `src/components/RecordsTable/RecordsTable.stories.tsx`
- `src/components/WinnersTable/WinnersTable.stories.tsx`
- `src/components/YearTable/YearTable.stories.tsx` (uses a related fixture — verify while fixing)
- `src/components/HomeContent/HomeContent.stories.tsx` (new, from SYS-600 — renders three `RecordsTable`s from this fixture simultaneously, so the warning fires 3x)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` entries have unique `id` values (and ideally non-identical `player`s, to make stories more visually representative).
- No "duplicate key" console error when running `npm run test:storybook` for the affected stories.
